summary: Iteration 11 - Phase 2 httpOnly cookie auth migration regression. Backend pytest 10/10 PASSED covering cookie issuance (HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax + Path=/), /me extraction matrix (cookie-only, header-only, no-auth=401, Bearer null=401, Bearer null + valid cookie = 200 cookie-wins), logout cookie clearing, role regression (data_entry/employee). Frontend Playwright validated: login sets HttpOnly cookie not visible to JS, localStorage.token=null + localStorage.user set, hard reload preserves session, direct /customers as admin works, logout (window.confirm accepted) calls /api/auth/logout 200 -> cookie cleared -> redirected /login -> /dashboard revisit redirects to /login (no infinite loop), employee lands on /daily-tasks and is blocked from /customers, data_entry sees Edit buttons (Phase 1 regression preserved).
action_items: Phase 2b cleanup (already noted by main agent, NOT a bug): some legacy pages still read localStorage.getItem('token') and send 'Authorization: Bearer null'; backend ignores 'Bearer null' and falls back to cookie so it works, but those call sites should be cleaned up.

Logout uses window.confirm() which is fine functionally but blocks headless tests by default; consider replacing with a styled confirm dialog (shadcn AlertDialog) for better UX consistency. NOT a regression - existing behavior.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py: 'Bearer null' is rejected by case-insensitive check ('null' / empty). Implementation is correct and well-commented. Consider also rejecting literal 'undefined' for completeness (frontend tooling sometimes serializes undefined as the string 'undefined').

auth_routes.py logout endpoint requires auth (Depends(get_current_user)). If a stale frontend without cookie clicks logout it will get 401 silently. Consider making logout idempotent (always return 200, always clear cookie) so the UX never hangs - but current behavior is acceptable since AuthContext also clears local state regardless.
Cookie config defaults AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE='true' which is correct for production HTTPS but will break local dev over plain http. Document this in README or .env.example.

axios.defaults.withCredentials = true is set globally; ensure no third-party axios calls (e.g., to public CDNs) are accidentally sending the cookie. Currently only same-origin /api calls are made so this is safe, but worth a defensive note.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Cookie auth file: /app/backend/tests/test_cookie_auth_iter11.py. Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_cookie_auth_iter11.py -v. Important Playwright caveat: the desktop logout button (data-testid='desktop-logout-btn') triggers a window.confirm; you MUST register page.on('dialog', lambda d: asyncio.create_task(d.accept())) before clicking, otherwise the confirm hangs and the click resolves with no API call. The HttpOnly cookie is verified via page.context.cookies() (httpOnly=True, sameSite='Lax', secure=True). document.cookie correctly does NOT contain auth_token. Bearer null requests with valid cookie correctly succeed (cookie wins) - this is by design while Phase 2b cleanup of legacy localStorage token reads is pending.
rca of the issue: N/A - no defects found. Phase 2 migration to httpOnly cookies is functioning correctly end-to-end. The earlier Test4 logout-UI failure in the first Playwright run was a TEST harness issue (window.confirm not auto-accepted), not a product bug - reproduced and resolved by registering a dialog handler.
